fields.label: Script Guidelines
fields.options:
Custom Script Guidelines

Available Context Variables:

context = {
    'message': {
        'content': 'message content',
        'type': 'message type',
        'from': 'sender number'
    },
    'command': 'current command'
}

Example Use Cases:

1. Send a Custom Response:

def execute(context):
    # Get the message content
    message = context['message']['content']
    sender = context['message']['from']
    
    # Send a custom response
    frappe.publish_realtime(
        'whatsapp_message',
        {
            'message': f'Custom response to: {message}',
            'to': sender
        }
    )

2. Database Operations:

def execute(context):
    # Create a log entry
    frappe.get_doc({
        'doctype': 'WhatsApp Log',
        'message': context['message']['content'],
        'sender': context['message']['from']
    }).insert()

3. External API Integration:

def execute(context):
    import requests
    
    # Call an external API
    response = requests.get(
        'https://api.example.com/data',
        params={'query': context['message']['content']}
    )
    
    # Process the response
    if response.status_code == 200:
        data = response.json()
        # Do something with the data

Available Frappe Functions:

  • frappe.get_doc(doctype, name)
  • frappe.get_value(doctype, name, fieldname)
  • frappe.get_all(doctype, filters={}, fields=[])
  • frappe.publish_realtime(event, message)
  • frappe.throw(msg)

Best Practices:

  • Always define an execute(context) function
  • Handle exceptions appropriately
  • Use frappe.log_error() for error logging
  • Add comments for complex logic
